body.title: perf: Use single PUT for small cloud uploads
body.body:
Closes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/28356

Performance: this PR will use a single PUT for small writes, reducing  the number of round-trips (from 3 to 1).

Note. With the decision to use single PUT vs Multipart now defered, any potential error condition may surface later. Fly-by: remove risk of calling flush on small part, which would trigger an `EntityTooSmall`, and other.

AI was used. I have reviewed and stand by the changes.

body.title: Single `PUT` for small uploads to cloud

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or an improvement of an existing feature

body.body:
### Description

The internal `CloudWriter` uses multipart upload for all files, even when small. This translates to a minimum of 3 round-trips, whereas a single `Put` would suffice.

Proposed solution: internally buffer up to the minimum size, and only switch to multipart upload when the size exceeds the minimum part limit (e.g., 5 MB).

body.title: perf: `LazyFrame.pivot` on hive partition is slower that looping on each partition

labels.name: P-goal
labels.description: Priority: aligns with long-term Polars goals

body.body:
Hey there! I'm hoping you can help me figure out whether what I'm seeing is expected and/or a known limitation. **Setup**: I have a long-format dataset written to a hive-partitioned parquet store (partitioned by `year/month/day`) with columns `datetime`, `variable`, `value`. I want to pivot it into wide format (one column per `variable`). I tried three shapes of the same query: 1. `bulk_fetch(datetime)`: single `scan_parquet` on the root, one pivot keyed on `datetime`. 2. `bulk_fetch(partition+datetime)`: same scan, pivot keyed on `[year, month, day, datetime]` (i.e. I hand the planner the hive keys as part of the index, hoping it uses them). 3. `loop_fetch`: iterate over each `year=*/month=*/day=*` directory in Python, pivot each independently, then `pl.concat`. Two things stand out to me: * As the number of unique elements in `on_columns` grows, the naive Python loop (`loop_fetch`) becomes the fastest strategy. * `bulk_fetch(partition+datetime)` is the slowest variation at every cardinality, even though passing the hive partition keys as part of the pivot index feels like it should let the planner do the per-partition pivot itself. #26207 might be related, however here the partitioning is implicit (hive layout). If that's the same root cause, great, feel free to close as a dup. ## Code Snippets Here is the implementation of `bulk_fetch` and `loop_fetch`. `bulk_fetch` is then called with `index = "datetime"` and `index=[*partitions, "datetime"]`. ```py def bulk_fetch(index: str | Sequence[str], n_columns: int) -> pl.DataFrame: return ( _fetch_path(path=TMP_DIR, index=index, n_columns=n_columns) .sort("datetime") .collect() ) def loop_fetch(n_columns: int) -> pl.DataFrame: # By sorting paths, the dataframes will return sorted by (year, month, day), # therefore we can sort each single dataframe by datetime singularly to # guarantee final sorting of the concatenated frame paths = natural_sort(TMP_DIR.glob("year=*/month=*/day=*")) return pl.concat( ( _fetch_path(path=path, index="datetime", n_columns=n_columns) .sort("datetime") .collect() for path in paths ), how="vertical", ) def _fetch_path(path: Path, index: str | Sequence[str], n_columns: int) -> pl.LazyFrame: on_columns = [f"col_{idx}" for idx in range(n_columns)] return ( pl.scan_parquet(path, schema=SCHEMA, hive_partitioning=True) .pivot( index=index, on="variable", on_columns=on_columns, values="value", aggregate_function="first", ) .select("datetime", *on_columns) ) def natural_sort(paths: Iterable[Path]) -> list[Path]: """Sort paths so e.g. "day=2" comes before "day=10".""" def _natural_key(path: Path) -> list[int | str]: return [ int(part) if part.isdigit() else part for part in re.split(r"(\d+)", str(path)) ] return sorted(paths, key=_natural_key) ``` ## Results in numbers ### 5 runs, 10 columns | Strategy | Engine | Mean | Median | Min | Max | Stdev | | ------------------------------ | --------- | ------: | ------: | ------: | -------: | ------: | | loop_fetch | cpu | 2.104 s | 2.090 s | 2.077 s | 2.141 s | 0.030 s | | bulk_fetch(datetime) | streaming | 2.217 s | 2.173 s | 2.061 s | 2.461 s | 0.149 s | | bulk_fetch(datetime) | cpu | 3.443 s | 3.429 s | 3.194 s | 3.854 s | 0.254 s | | loop_fetch | streaming | 3.566 s | 3.575 s | 3.535 s | 3.582 s | 0.019 s | | bulk_fetch(partition+datetime) | cpu | 6.211 s | 6.135 s | 5.980 s | 6.540 s | 0.230 s | | bulk_fetch(partition+datetime) | streaming | 9.347 s | 9.272 s | 8.932 s | 10.077 s | 0.431 s | ### 5 runs, 50 columns | Strategy | Engine | Mean | Median | Min | Max | Stdev | | -------------------- | --------- | -------: | -------: | -------: | -------: | ------: | | loop_fetch | cpu | 8.912 s | 8.742 s | 8.669 s | 9.281 s | 0.293 s | | loop_fetch | streaming | 16.927 s | 16.909 s | 16.782 s | 17.108 s | 0.124 s | | bulk_fetch(datetime) | streaming | 52.294 s | 52.391 s | 41.451 s | 61.588 s | 7.311 s | ### 5 runs, 80 columns | Strategy | Engine | Mean | Median | Min | Max | Stdev | | -------------------- | --------- | --------: | --------: | --------: | --------: | ------: | | loop_fetch | cpu | 19.492 s | 19.486 s | 19.409 s | 19.548 s | 0.058 s | | loop_fetch | streaming | 35.795 s | 35.781 s | 35.390 s | 36.200 s | 0.289 s | | bulk_fetch(datetime) | streaming | 148.901 s | 148.693 s | 143.127 s | 153.857 s | 4.775 s | ## Full benchmark repro Here is the script I used for the benchmark (you can `uv run .py`). > [!CAUTION] > The script requires to write to a directory created via `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="polars-bench-")`
Benchmarking script

```py # /// script # requires-python = ">=3.12" # dependencies = [ # "polars==1.39.3", # "cyclopts==4.7.0", # "rich==14.3.3", # ] # /// from __future__ import annotations import re import tempfile from statistics import fmean, median, stdev import time from datetime import datetime from pathlib import Path from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Annotated, Callable, Literal import polars as pl from cyclopts import App, Parameter from rich.console import Console from rich.table import Table if TYPE_CHECKING: from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence PARTITION_KEY = { "year": pl.col("datetime").dt.year(), "month": pl.col("datetime").dt.month(), "day": pl.col("datetime").dt.day(), } SCHEMA = pl.Schema( { "datetime": pl.Datetime(time_unit="us", time_zone=None), "variable": pl.String(), "value": pl.Int64(), } ) type Engine = Literal["streaming", "cpu"] type PolarsEngine = Literal["streaming", "in-memory"] _ENGINE_MAP: dict[Engine, PolarsEngine] = { "streaming": "streaming", "cpu": "in-memory", } def fake_dataset( start: datetime = datetime(2020, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0), end: datetime = datetime(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0), interval: str = "10s", n_columns: int = 10, ) -> pl.LazyFrame: datetimes = pl.datetime_range( start=start, end=end, interval=interval, closed="left" ) return pl.concat( ( pl.LazyFrame() .select(datetime=datetimes.sample(fraction=0.9, shuffle=True, seed=42)) .with_columns( variable=pl.lit(f"col_{idx}"), value=pl.int_range(pl.len()), ) for idx in range(n_columns) ), how="vertical", ) def _fetch_path(path: Path, index: str | Sequence[str], n_columns: int) -> pl.LazyFrame: on_columns = [f"col_{idx}" for idx in range(n_columns)] return ( pl.scan_parquet(path, schema=SCHEMA, hive_partitioning=True) .pivot( index=index, on="variable", on_columns=on_columns, values="value", aggregate_function="first", ) .select("datetime", *on_columns) ) def bulk_fetch( tmp_dir: Path, index: str | Sequence[str], n_columns: int ) -> pl.DataFrame: return ( _fetch_path(path=tmp_dir, index=index, n_columns=n_columns) .sort("datetime") .collect() ) def natural_sort(paths: Iterable[Path]) -> list[Path]: """Sort paths so e.g. "day=2" comes before "day=10".""" def _natural_key(path: Path) -> list[int | str]: return [ int(part) if part.isdigit() else part for part in re.split(r"(\d+)", str(path)) ] return sorted(paths, key=_natural_key) def loop_fetch(tmp_dir: Path, n_columns: int) -> pl.DataFrame: paths = natural_sort(tmp_dir.glob("year=*/month=*/day=*")) return pl.concat( ( _fetch_path(path=path, index="datetime", n_columns=n_columns) .sort("datetime") .collect() for path in paths ), how="vertical", ) def _time_once(build: Callable[[], pl.DataFrame], engine: Engine) -> float: t0 = time.perf_counter() with pl.Config(set_engine_affinity=_ENGINE_MAP[engine]): _ = build() return time.perf_counter() - t0 def _fmt(seconds: float) -> str: return f"{seconds:,.3f} s" _HEADERS = ("Strategy", "Engine", "Mean", "Median", "Min", "Max", "Stdev") def _summarize( results: dict[tuple[str, Engine], list[float]], ) -> list[tuple[str, Engine, float, float, float, float, float]]: return sorted( ( ( strategy, engine, fmean(times), median(times), min(times), max(times), stdev(times) if len(times) > 1 else 0.0, ) for (strategy, engine), times in results.items() ), key=lambda r: r[3], ) def _render_table( results: dict[tuple[str, Engine], list[float]], n_runs: int, n_columns: int, ) -> Table: max_strategy = max(len(s) for s, _ in results) table = Table( title=f"Polars fetch benchmark — {n_runs} runs, {n_columns} columns", show_lines=True, ) table.add_column(_HEADERS[0], style="bold cyan", min_width=max_strategy) table.add_column(_HEADERS[1], style="magenta") table.add_column(_HEADERS[2], justify="right", style="blue") table.add_column(_HEADERS[3], justify="right", style="yellow") table.add_column(_HEADERS[4], justify="right", style="green") table.add_column(_HEADERS[5], justify="right", style="red") table.add_column(_HEADERS[6], justify="right") for st, eng, mean, med, _min, _max, std in _summarize(results): table.add_row(st, eng, _fmt(mean), _fmt(med), _fmt(_min), _fmt(_max), _fmt(std)) return table app = App(help="Benchmark polars fetch strategies over a partitioned parquet dataset.") @app.default def run( n_runs: Annotated[ int, Parameter(help="Number of timed runs per (strategy, engine).") ] = 5, n_columns: Annotated[ tuple[int, ...], Parameter(help="One or more `col_i` counts; one benchmark table per value."), ] = (10, 50, 80), engines: Annotated[ tuple[Engine, ...], Parameter(help="Polars collect engines to benchmark."), ] = ("streaming", "cpu"), warmup: Annotated[int, Parameter(help="Warm-up runs discarded before timing.")] = 1, ) -> None: """Generate a partitioned parquet dataset and benchmark three fetch strategies.""" console = Console() if n_runs < 1: raise ValueError("n_runs must be >= 1") if not n_columns: raise ValueError("n_columns must contain at least one value") for n_cols in n_columns: with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="polars-bench-") as tmp_name: tmp_dir = Path(tmp_name) strategies: dict[str, Callable[[], pl.DataFrame]] = { "loop_fetch": lambda n=n_cols, d=tmp_dir: loop_fetch( tmp_dir=d, n_columns=n ), "bulk_fetch(datetime)": lambda n=n_cols, d=tmp_dir: bulk_fetch( tmp_dir=d, index="datetime", n_columns=n ), } if n_cols < 25: strategies["bulk_fetch(partition+datetime)"] = ( lambda n=n_cols, d=tmp_dir: bulk_fetch( tmp_dir=d, index=[*PARTITION_KEY, "datetime"], n_columns=n ) ) console.log( f"writing dataset with {n_cols} columns to [bold]{tmp_dir}[/bold]…" ) fake_dataset(n_columns=n_cols).sink_parquet( path=pl.PartitionBy(tmp_dir, key=PARTITION_KEY, include_key=False) ) results: dict[tuple[str, Engine], list[float]] = {} total = len(strategies) * len(engines) * (warmup + n_runs) with console.status("[bold green]benchmarking…") as status: done = 0 for strategy_name, build in strategies.items(): for engine in engines: if ( n_cols >= 50 and engine == "cpu" and strategy_name.startswith("bulk") ): continue for _ in range(warmup): _time_once(build, engine) done += 1 status.update( f"[bold green]{strategy_name} / {engine} " f"(n_columns={n_cols}) — warmup ({done}/{total})" ) times: list[float] = [] for run_idx in range(n_runs): elapsed = _time_once(build, engine) times.append(elapsed) done += 1 status.update( f"[bold green]{strategy_name} / {engine} " f"(n_columns={n_cols}) — " f"run {run_idx + 1}/{n_runs} ({_fmt(elapsed)})" ) results[(strategy_name, engine)] = times console.print(_render_table(results, n_runs=n_runs, n_columns=n_cols)) if __name__ == "__main__": app() ```

## Installed versions ```terminal --------Version info--------- Polars: 1.39.3 Index type: UInt32 Platform: macOS-26.4.1-arm64-arm-64bit Python: 3.12.13 (main, Mar 25 2026, 03:16:06) [Clang 22.1.1 ] Runtime: rt32 ----Optional dependencies---- None ```

body.title: Inconsistent application of hive keys when using scan_parquet
body.body:
Hi,

### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"d": pl.arange(0, 10_000, eager=True)}).with_columns(a=pl.col("d") % 100, b=pl.col("d") % 100 + 42)
df.write_parquet("tmp.parquet", use_pyarrow=True, pyarrow_options={"partition_cols": ["a", "b"]})

print("partition selected")
print(pl.scan_parquet("tmp.parquet/**/*.parquet").filter((pl.col("a") == 10) & (pl.col("b") == 52)).explain())
print(pl.scan_parquet("tmp.parquet/**/*.parquet").filter(pl.col("a") == 10).filter(pl.col("b") == 52).explain())
print("partition not selected")
print(pl.scan_parquet("tmp.parquet/**/*.parquet").filter([pl.col("a") == 10, pl.col("b") == 52]).explain())
print(pl.scan_parquet("tmp.parquet/**/*.parquet").filter(pl.col("a") == 10, pl.col("b") == 52).explain())
print(pl.scan_parquet("tmp.parquet/**/*.parquet").filter(a=10, b=52).explain())
```


### Log output

```shell
partition selected

  Parquet SCAN tmp.parquet\a=10\b=52\98e9b3fb79214841a5531034c1507a6b-0.parquet
  PROJECT */3 COLUMNS
  SELECTION: [([(col("a")) == (10)]) & ([(col("b")) == (52)])]

  Parquet SCAN tmp.parquet\a=10\b=52\98e9b3fb79214841a5531034c1507a6b-0.parquet
  PROJECT */3 COLUMNS
  SELECTION: [([(col("b")) == (52)]) & ([(col("a")) == (10)])]
partition not selected

  Parquet SCAN 100 files: first file: tmp.parquet\a=0\b=42\98e9b3fb79214841a5531034c1507a6b-0.parquet
  PROJECT */3 COLUMNS
  SELECTION: [([(col("a")) == (10)].cast(Boolean)) & ([(col("b")) == (52)].cast(Boolean))]

  Parquet SCAN 100 files: first file: tmp.parquet\a=0\b=42\98e9b3fb79214841a5531034c1507a6b-0.parquet
  PROJECT */3 COLUMNS
  SELECTION: [([(col("a")) == (10)].cast(Boolean)) & ([(col("b")) == (52)].cast(Boolean))]

  Parquet SCAN 100 files: first file: tmp.parquet\a=0\b=42\98e9b3fb79214841a5531034c1507a6b-0.parquet
  PROJECT */3 COLUMNS
  SELECTION: [([(col("a")) == (10)].cast(Boolean)) & ([(col("b")) == (52)].cast(Boolean))]
```


### Issue description

Depending on the form of the filter call polars propagates the condition to the hive partitioning values or not. This makes for confusing behaviour since it's not mentioned anywhere.

### Expected behavior

Te condition are propagated to the hive partitioning regardless of how the filter call form.

Or at least the limitation should be documented


This may be somewhat connected with https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/12932
